claims.claim: **For children beyond the newborn period.** Use specialised guidance for neonates, long-term NG feeding, and diabetes, cardiac, metabolic or renal conditions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use the enteral route (oral or NG) whenever possible; shocked children need IV resuscitation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute fluid change is best tracked by serial weights**; clinical signs are often imprecise. **Rehydration does not treat the cause** — review regularly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **NG beats IV on safety**, electrolyte risk and recovery speed from gastroenteritis, and can deliver EBM or formula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Indications:** rehydration after GI losses or sustained poor intake; replacing usual intake in acute illness (e.g. bronchiolitis, gingivostomatitis); replacing ongoing losses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contraindications:** nil by mouth/fasting · shock or critically unwell · possible bowel obstruction (bilious vomiting, severe distension, ileus) · altered conscious state or aspiration risk · facial trauma or suspected base-of-skull fracture.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss with a senior clinician:** age under 6 months · severe dehydration, electrolyte abnormality or hypoglycaemia · high ADH risk (acute CNS or significant pulmonary conditions) · short gut or chronic GI disorder · craniofacial abnormality.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usually no investigations.** Consider glucose and electrolytes in young infants, significant ongoing losses, or NG support continuing past the first 4–6 hour rehydration phase — **ORS is hypotonic and hyponatraemia can occur.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rehydrate with ORS in all children over 1 month**; available ORS brands do not differ in a clinically significant way.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After rehydration, milk-fed infants resume their usual EBM or formula** (orally or NG). **Stop fortification in GI illness** — the osmotic load can worsen diarrhoea.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **2/3 maintenance suits most unwell children needing hydration support**, especially respiratory and CNS infections. **Full maintenance** for well children not drinking enough (e.g. fasting for surgery) and the maintenance phase of gastroenteritis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Full maintenance (4:2:1):** 3–10 kg 100 mL/kg/day (4 mL/kg/hr) · 10–20 kg 1000 + 50 × (weight − 10) mL/day [40 + 2 × (weight − 10) mL/hr] · 20–60 kg 1500 + 20 × (weight − 20) mL/day [60 + 1 × (weight − 20) mL/hr] · over 60 kg normal maximum 2400 mL/day (100 mL/hr).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not prescribe maintenance from infant milk volumes (150–200 mL/kg/day)** — those meet growth needs in well babies, not fluid needs in unwell ones.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For moderate dehydration in common illnesses such as gastroenteritis**, to speed discharge home.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Not suitable for:** dehydration from lower respiratory infection, meningitis or significant electrolyte abnormality · **age under 6 months** · significant comorbidity · abdominal pain. **Severe dehydration needs IV fluid resuscitation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ORS at 10–25 mL/kg/hr, over 4 hours.** Evidence supports 25 mL/kg/hr; some centres use 10–12.5 mL/kg/hr.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Many NG pumps max out at 300 mL/hr** — divide the target volume by 300 mL (e.g. 1800 mL for an 18 kg child runs as 300 mL/hr for 6 hours).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Preferred for moderate dehydration where rapid volumes are inappropriate.** First 24 hours: **replace a 5% deficit over the first 6 hours**, reassess, then run the daily maintenance volume across the following 18 hours; next 24 hours: remaining deficit if still needed, plus maintenance.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Return quickly to normal fluids and food; keep breastfeeding.** No benefit from gradual milk reintroduction or dilute feeds. If diarrhoea worsens with lactose or fructose, consider 1–2 weeks of lactose-free milk and no fruit/juice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Replace ongoing losses mL for mL with ORS**, on top of maintenance (e.g. 200 mL of diarrhoea over 4 hours → ORS 50 mL/hr for the next 4 hours).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weigh at the start and at least daily**; document inputs and losses (including urine) with at least 12-hourly subtotals.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Vomiting: temporarily slow the fluids; consider ondansetron from 6 months of age.** Significant abdominal pain or ongoing vomiting: senior review.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** for severe dehydration or electrolyte/glucose abnormalities.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nasogastric fluids' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nasogastric_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23
